root_cause.text: The MPTCP subflow simultaneous-connect fallback relied on subflow_state_change()/sk_state_change to detect the condition, but a TCP subflow can receive the simult-connect SYN-ACK after entering FIN_WAIT1, a transition that does not invoke that callback, so the fallback is skipped and the MPTCP socket state becomes inconsistent.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “the sk_state_change() callback is not invoked for * -> FIN_WAIT1 transitions,” causing the SYN-ACK to “bypass[] the MPTCP fallback check,” and the patch fixes this by moving the check from subflow_state_change() into mptcp_syn_options() “at syn-ack generation time,” while removing the old fallback block from subflow_state_change().

intent_record.intent_summary: Detect simultaneous connect during MPTCP SYN option setup and force fallback while suppressing further MPC handshake processing.
intent_record.what: Inside mptcp_syn_options(), a new early conditional was added under the existing subflow->request_mptcp check to detect subflow_simultaneous_connect(sk); in that case it emits WARN_ON_ONCE if mptcp_try_fallback(sk, MPTCP_MIB_SIMULTCONNFALLBACK) fails, clears subflow->request_mptcp, and returns false before setting MPC SYN options.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when an MPTCP subflow hits a simultaneous-connect scenario during SYN option generation, the code now abandons MPTCP option setup and forces fallback handling instead of continuing with the MPC handshake path; clearing request_mptcp also prevents mptcp_finish_connect() from later processing the handshake incorrectly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict simultaneous-connect detection to active subflows in TCP_SYN_RECV so later socket states are no longer misclassified.
intent_record.what: The function subflow_simultaneous_connect() was changed from returning a bitmask-based check over multiple socket states (TCP_ESTABLISHED, TCP_FIN_WAIT1, TCP_FIN_WAIT2, TCP_CLOSING) combined with is_active_ssk(subflow) and !subflow->conn_finished, to returning only whether sk->sk_state == TCP_SYN_RECV and is_active_ssk(subflow); a comment was also added stating that the socket state implies !subflow->conn_finished.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now reports simultaneous connect only for active subflows in the TCP_SYN_RECV state instead of for several later connection and closing states. This narrows the condition, preventing sockets in established or teardown states from being treated as simultaneous-connect cases and relying on the state check to make the conn_finished test unnecessary.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove simultaneous-connect fallback handling from subflow_state_change() to avoid triggering that recovery path and state propagation in the wrong execution path.
intent_record.what: The change removes an entire conditional block from subflow_state_change() that checked subflow_simultaneous_connect(sk) and, when true, called mptcp_try_fallback(sk, MPTCP_MIB_SIMULTCONNFALLBACK), set subflow->conn_finished = 1, and invoked mptcp_propagate_state(parent, sk, subflow, NULL).
intent_record.how: At runtime, subflow_state_change() no longer performs immediate simultaneous-connect fallback handling in this code path, so it stops forcing fallback, marking the subflow connection as finished, and propagating state changes when subflow_simultaneous_connect(sk) is detected here. This prevents that special-case behavior from occurring at this point in execution.
